item.title: SCP seeking greenlight- Ancient Nautiloids
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: 4 unseen ancient lineages of nautiloids are found around the Atlantic Ocean. Each one is drastically different from the other. Though interact with each other rarely, on an instance of each lineage will head for the Bermuda Triangle for a deathmatch for fertility rights.

+ Central
- Central

Central Narrative: Four undiscovered nautiloids species were discovered fighting in the middle of the Bermuda Triangle by an international oceanography survey. They were later discovered in different parts of the Atlantics with little overlap in population overlap.

Every 10 years, a ritual of fertility will be held by each instance of SCP-XXXX at the center of the Bermuda Triangle. The ritual ends until the last instance is alive. The sole survivor of the ritual, for example, an instance of SCP-XXXX-B, will have a population boom of three years for its instance.

+ Hook
- Hook

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Humans know more of what’s above them than what’s below the deep oceans. The oceans are scary indeed. About 90-97% of the ocean is still undiscovered. The ocean is the last frontier to travel on this planet. Many creatures are left undiscovered to this day.

Additional Notes: Draft is complete. Sketches for SCP instances are finished

item.title: Re: A small question
item.content:encoded:
Does anyone know why this is said,

Because readers don't find the material interesting? If something doesn't interest them on the mainsite, they're not obligated to explain exactly why the piece didn't spark their interest. If someone is expecting thorough critique from a reviewer, the forums and IRC chatrooms are the place to look.

because I am curious as to whether this helpful to the author

While it's not the most helpful feedback, it's more helpful than nothing at all. Disliking something for not being interesting enough is different from disliking something for being too long-winded and a slog to read, or disliking something because it uses a color scheme or unique format that is disorienting or difficult to follow.

as one person could find it disinterestong but the next could find it absolutely fascinating.

Just because some people find something interesting does not mean everyone else has to feel the same way, and vice versa. People can disagree with others about the kind of article they like to read. Sometimes an author has to just shrug and accept a downvote. Just because someone else likes something does not make it wrong to dislike the same thing for personal preference reasons.

item.title: Re: Deer in the mist (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Just a heads up, we already have SCP-3502 (The Kangaroo Sign) which plays on the same premise of "animals that are often hit by people in vehicles get their revenge on said vehicles and people" but does not rely on the shock horror of deaths.

What you have here feels like a fairly common urban legend, which might be workable based on the imagery of the deer (though we already have some well-known anomalous deer on the mainsite (you can see them in this listing: http://www.scpwiki.com/system:page-tags/tag/cervine) but is also kind of bland given that it relies on typical horror genre tropes like the mysterious mist, accidentally harming allies/family while trying to harm something else(the movie Oculus ends with this), and the overly convenient found journal.

Personally I recommend delving more into the lore of the deer from a different perspective, maybe a colony of wildlife creatures who consider it their guardian, or the like. A Group of Interest article might be a better format for something like this.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No, I would like feedback.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The Modification Shop is a shop that will keep on growing from only Human Modification to cars, guns, and more. The shop is run by a machine and the shop has a invisible barrier that will not allow you to leave if have any not paid for items on you or if you have not paid yet. The things you buy from the shop are modifications that will be used as modules for the system when the subject is placed inside a tube, one of the modules makes the space of the module capacity bigger. It starts at 3 and the module will use one space and will add 3 spaces. The shop will make its own prices as you buy the items and it must be paid in full within 24 hours or the people in the shop at that time will be released and the shop will close for 1 week. The prices of the shop's items can be bargained and the foundation usually uses it to generate their military or D-Class. item.title: Just trying to be cool again
item.content:encoded:
So after spending a considerable amount of time in IRC chat, I've come to notice a few things. A lot of people are more concerned with getting their ideas greenlit as opposed to crafting a good story. This is not the case for everyone, let me just preface that, but I do see it happen a fair amount of times.

This thought process is really upsetting to me. Why should anyone else's opinion be disregarded just because they can't give you a green light? Why would you think that your own thoughts are inadequate just because you can't give someone a greenlight? Doesn't make any sense to me, yet this seems to be the thought process for a lot of new authors on site. And many of them get discouraged and leave if their first idea doesn't work out.

Anyway, the preamble is over. I'm trying to convey all these emotions and such in the third tab of this sandbox. I'm really struggling with the subtlety of this one.

Forum thread: Just trying to be cool again

item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the fast response!

The idea was to have the object seem fairly straight forward at first. Testing would begin with simple yes-no questions then research staff begins to explore its applications.

I have revised my idea a little to make an SCP classification more appropriate.

Incident report: #████-██

After a breach of security, SCP-XXXX is used in interrogation to verify information, the log is swiftly cut after the interview subject starts asking sensitive questions regarding [Data Expunged]. While no answers were given it is clear the subject planned to exploit SCP-XXXX's anomalous properties.

When interrogation ended as security came to take SCP-XXXX into containment SCP-XXXX began to produce the truth reaction continuously until interrogation subject [Data Expunged] was escorted out of the research chamber.

How SCP-XXXX produced the truth reaction without a completed trigger is unknown.

Recommendation: restrict testing with SCP-XXXX to prevent further information leaks.

item.title: Re: Who Hired Ralph Roget?
item.content:encoded:
Roget isn't incompetent; he's actually very good at a lot of stuff, he's very clever and committed to the Foundation. He's young, and he has impatient tendencies, and he gets a lot of flack for his grandmother being the Site Director, and she comes down hard on him because he's her grandson and she wants him to succeed. It's a complex dynamic; Roget himself handles it extremely well in his tales, and I was just hoping to capture some of it here. The vibe I get from Roget is that he's super smart and eager, but can be pushed to rash moments in conversation or even rash actions because of inexperience.

Glad you liked it overall; I liked it too, the first time I wrote it, and then I had to rewrite it like fifteen times to cover all these goddamn bases. Fascism losing is always pleasant escapism, isn't it?

And yeah, that quote is as close as I'll ever get to referencing… what it's referencing. Please nobody reference what it's referencing directly!

Thanks a bunch :)

item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the crit.

I originally thought of this for the SCP. Could you let me know your thought?

+ The Story I had in mind 
- Collapsed

A person is being targeted by the entity. They keep blacking out for longer and longer. At first it’s only a short bit, regaining consciousness after a minute or so. But it keeps getting longer, and they have no memory to recall what happened during these blackouts.
They seek therapy, which fails and then onto medicine which also does nothing. Mystics and psychics next which do nothing as well, all the time they’re having blackouts and using what little time they do have to work out what’s going on.
Finally, they cease, all of these professionals forget about the interactions. The only thing that they find is random prescriptions to a person that doesn’t exist.
During this time, the victim is constantly paranoid and violent between the blackouts. Family and friends worry for them, but eventually become estranged because of these violent outbursts. This leads to the victim being fired from work, broke and without emotional support.

The foundation discovers that doctors are looking into why prescriptions for nonexistent people are being made. The foundation intervenes, administering amnestics and begin a search for the entity.

item.title: Who Hired Ralph Roget?
item.content:encoded:
One thing that struck me as strange was that Dr. Roget has such a high position given even his grandmother admits he's pretty incompetent. The Foundation didn't strike me as the kind of organization that would accept that kind of nepotism.

Without so much as a knock beforehand, the door to his grandmother's office swung open. "Site Director," he whined, glancing up. He pointed at the shiny new nameplate on his grandmother's desk. "Site Director."

I had to read that paragraph several times before I understood that he was petulantly demanding to be called site director. It might be the phrasing, but part of me couldn't believe how childish he was. Is there lore I'm missing about how he got to be where he is?

Overall though, this was a lot of fun. Love wins, demonic fascists lose, and it was a clever use of the SCP-5109 and Doug.
Also:

"'You're fired'? Seriously?" Phil croaked.
Amelia smiled, massaging his neck. "I associate it with fascism, now. Anyway, it worked.

Perfection.

item.title: Multicolor EpiPen | Greenlight Requested
item.content:encoded:
An object that functions like an EpiPen and uses the liquid it injects to alter the user's emotions by taking and replacing their brain's proteins from the limbic system.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 90 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An object with an exterior resembling a multicolor pen and a mechanism resembling an epinephrine autoinjector. Multiple different-colored tabs near the top of the pen help the user locate which emotion they are looking to alter. A stadium-shaped cutout reveals a cylinder that swivels to match which tab has been pressed, giving the tab its name: weariness, lustfulness, happiness, sadness, irritableness, or frightfulness. A label on one side of the pen details the instructions for use. This object is reusable as it "recycles" previously exchanged proteins.

When injected into the deltoid, preferably the left, intelligent cells follow the user's blood flow to the brain and exchange emotion-effecting proteins with the limbic system. After the exchange has been made, the cells follow the blood flow through the heart and back to the inserted needle to recycle the collected proteins. After use, the user should have the opposite emotion to what they had originally. (Each tab has its opposite.)

+ Reveal Hidden Text
- Hide Hidden Text

Central Narrative: The object was discovered on █/█/███ in ███████, Alabama by a man named ███ ████████. He had discovered the object in his deceased father's home while preparing for an estate sale and pocketed it believing the object was an unused epinephrine autoinjector due to the instructions listed on the side of the pen that are "similar-looking from a distance". At a grocery store that afternoon, ████████ had sampled a ██████ brand cookie, only to undergo an allergic reaction to the nuts it contained. He retrieved the object from his pocket and had evidently pressed a random tab out of confusion before injecting the liquid into the side of his thigh. After undergoing investigation, ████████ was revealed to have injected himself with the "irritableness" serum. When paramedics located him, he was incredibly frightful of them and tried to escape unsuccessfully. The local authorities handed the pen over to the Foundation after being unable to identify the substances within the object and overall deeming it "potentially malicious". ████████ has since recovered from the incident.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This object could either be incredibly helpful or mind-breakingly dangerous. When you prepare to use the pen, you must press the tab of the emotion that you currently have - never the emotion you are hoping to gain. If the wrong tab is chosen, effects could range from fatigue to manic depression. This is due to the cells being unable to retrieve the incorrect proteins yet still drop off the ones it contains, and an emotional clash proceeds it.

Additional Notes:

  • I will not refer to the object as an EpiPen in the actual article. It is only in the title to help users get an idea of what the object looks like and how it generally works before reading.
  • I did my research about the science used by this object, though that is no guarantee that it is correct. Please help me to fix any errors you come across.
  • This is my first concept post for this site. I apologize for any misused/missing lingo.

item.title: Re: The Laughing Tree
item.content:encoded:
I want to show the emotional consequences of hazing.

The 1st and 2nd interviews show the beginning: a child that is surrounded by peers who see him as "the other" and adults that laugh at him while doing nothing. But there is a difference here, he isn't irreparably scarred by the tree. He cries and feels shame about what happened.

The 3rd interview shows the worst possible end: an adult who feels pleasure and mirth by watching children go through the same experience he did. His name scarred the tree as it did him. When his pain is eventually revealed, he will laugh at it, just as he did during the child's "tying."

Overall thoughts
For the most part I second caspian2, I like the concept as a whole, and the possible directions this could take. However there isn't anything inherently interesting or unique done with the narrative.

As it stands, the narrative doesn't really show a clear conflict, any driving force as to why the Foundation would want to learn more about the skip, (or why they might want to utilise it), there doesn't really seem to be any characters either.- which makes the narrative hard to get invested in emotionally, as there isn't much being shown other than the effects.

Along with this, there isn't really any clear end goal here, or much that expands on the questions raised in the concept. The narrative doesn't really seem to be building up to anything.- which (at least to me), makes the narrative as a whole feel a bit directionless, the object is just kinda here?

I feel for this work, you would need to show a stronger conflict, and show some sort of character arc. Rather than just having the narrative showcase the skips effects. Along with this, I would recommend focusing a bit more on the skips possible origin/purpose or the possible ways the Foundation might utilise the skip.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight

item.title: Re: Skeleton's Daycare
item.content:encoded:
It's a cute concept, for sure! Though, the whole "earthquake" thing doesn't make much sense to me. I feel that if we got more detail into what the alien children are, more specifically, what their species is and how they behave, it might help bring the concept to light a bit more. Right now, all we have to go off of is cranky alien children of some kind that can make earthquakes. We definitely need a bit more info here.

Another thing I'm curious about is why the alien parents (I'm assuming they came from another plant) came to Earth and chose this one specific daycare to drop their children off. Why not use an alien daycare on their own planet? Why were the children accepted so calmly to begin with, seeing as aliens would normally cause people to panic? Can the aliens shapeshift, are aliens normal in this particular society, or is there another explanation?

The crystals, as well, need a greater explanation. Why did taking just one crystal away cause "the skeleton's life to become much harder"? Why did the aliens bring them to begin with? Why did they take them away?

One more thing - why did the daycare worker become a skeleton to begin with? There is no specification of time here. Did he truly work years and years watching these children, or was he an old man from the get-go?

Overall, this is a neat concept! I just feel like a bit more detail to fill in the gaps and explain things to the reader would be very helpful in this situation. (And I apologize if this review was not helpful since I included lots of "questions" - this is the first one I've written on this site.)

item.title: Re: [Seeking Greenlights] Retribution Gun
item.content:encoded:
Hello Traloc_Dheckoa! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a BB toy gun. When someone shoots the gun at someone else, the person who has been shot will show high levels of hostility towards the shooter, and try to take SCP-XXXX from the shooter. If the person that has been shot manages to retrieve the gun from the shooter, he or she will shoot it at the person who shot first, and in this case an actual bullet will be fired instead of a BB toy bullet, killing the initial shooter. The second shooter will then lose consciousness.

Overall, this feels a bit close to a "thing that dose a thing". As the skip has a bunch of effects, and no real purpose. Currently it just feels like some random object, with no context. Along with this, the effects shown aren't particularly interesting as it everything essentially boils down to "gun that shoots a real bullet". -getting angry and trying to take the gun over being shot, sounds like a pretty normal response. BB guns aren't allowed where I'm from, so I don't have much to go off. However, I have heard they can cause injuries (and apparently they hurt a lot).

Here are some of main questions:
Why does the skip shoot a real bullet? why does it cause people to become so aggressive? why does the 'shooter' become unconscious afterward? why was it made? what about the concept will make me as the reader invested?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The gun was taken from a crime scene where a 10-yo boy killed his friend while playing with toy guns, one of which was SCP-XXXX.

This is far too vague for the narrative, as there isn't any clear arc or conflict shown here. How did the Foundation get involved? who are the characters? what is the main conflict? how does the story end, and how should that make me feel?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.
